title: Song of Songs 1:1 (#1)
content:
Who is the writer of Song of Songs?

Solomon is the writer of Song of Songs.

title: Song of Songs 1:2 (#1)
content:
What does the young woman ask her lover to do?

The young woman asks her lover to kiss her with the kisses of his mouth.

title: Song of Songs 1:2 (#2)
content:
What does the young woman say is better than wine?

The young woman says her lover’s love is better than wine.

title: Song of Songs 1:3 (#1)
content:
What does the young woman say her lover’s name is like?

The young woman says his name is like fragrant oil.

title: Song of Songs 1:4 (#1)
content:
Where has the king brought the young woman?

The king has brought the young woman into his rooms.

title: Song of Songs 1:5 (#1)
content:
How does the young woman describe her skin?

The young woman describes her skin as dark but lovely like tents of Kedar, like curtains of Solomon.

title: Song of Songs 1:6 (#1)
content:
Why does she not want the other women to stare at her?

She does not want the other women to stare at her because her skin is scorched.

title: Song of Songs 1:6 (#2)
content:
What did the young woman’s brothers do when they were angry with her?

The young woman’s brothers made her a keeper of the vineyards.

title: Song of Songs 1:7 (#1)
content:
What does the woman ask her lover?

She asks him where he feeds his flock and where he rests his flock at noontime.

title: Song of Songs 1:8 (#1)
content:
How does her lover say the young woman can find him?

He tells her to follow the tracks of his flock to the shepherds’ tents.

title: Song of Songs 1:9 (#1)
content:
To what does the young woman’s lover compare her?

He compares her to a mare among Pharaoh’s chariots.

title: Song of Songs 1:10 (#1)
content:
What does her lover say is on her cheeks and neck?

He says earrings are on her cheeks and strings of jewels are on her neck.

title: Song of Songs 1:11 (#1)
content:
What does her lover say he will make for her?

He says he will make for her gold earrings with silver studs.

title: Song of Songs 1:12 (#1)
content:
Where was the king lying while the woman’s perfume spread in the room?

The king was lying on his couch while the fragrance of the woman’s perfume spread.

title: Song of Songs 1:13 (#1)
content:
Where does her beloved spend the night?

Her beloved spends the night lying between her breasts.

title: Song of Songs 1:14 (#1)
content:
To what does the young woman liken her beloved?

Her beloved is like a cluster of henna flowers in the vineyards of En Gedi.

title: Song of Songs 1:15 (#1)
content:
How does her lover describe her eyes?

He says her eyes are like doves.

title: Song of Songs 1:16 (#1)
content:
What does the woman say serves as their bed?

Leafy plants serve as their bed.

title: Song of Songs 1:17 (#1)
content:
Of what does the woman say the beams and rafters of their house are made?

The beams and rafters are made of cedar and pine trees.

title: Song of Songs 2:1 (#1)
content:
How does the woman describe herself?

She describes herself as a flower of the plain, a lily of the valleys.

title: Song of Songs 2:2 (#1)
content:
What does the man say she was like among the daughters of his countrymen?

He said she was like a lily among thorns.

title: Song of Songs 2:3 (#3)
content:
What was sweet to her taste?

His fruit was sweet to her taste.

title: Song of Songs 2:3 (#2)
content:
Where did the woman sit?

She sat down under his shadow with great delight.

title: Song of Songs 2:3 (#1)
content:
How does the woman describe her beloved among the young men?

The woman describes her young man as an apple tree among the trees of the forest.

title: Song of Songs 2:4 (#2)
content:
What was his banner over her?

His banner over her was love.

title: Song of Songs 2:4 (#1)
content:
Where did her young man bring her?

Her young man brought her to the house of wine.

title: Song of Songs 2:5 (#1)
content:
What does the young woman want to sustain and refresh herself?

The young woman wants raisin cakes to sustain her and apples to refresh her.

title: Song of Songs 2:6 (#1)
content:
Where is the young man’s left and right hands?

His left hand is under her head and his right hand embraces her.

title: Song of Songs 2:7 (#1)
content:
What does the young woman want the daughters of Jerusalem to avoid?

The young woman wants the young women to avoid awakening love before the right time comes.

title: Song of Songs 2:8 (#2)
content:
What does she say her beloved is doing?

He is leaping over the mountains and jumping over the hills.

title: Song of Songs 2:8 (#1)
content:
What sound does the young woman hear?

The young woman hears the voice of her beloved.

title: Song of Songs 2:9 (#1)
content:
What does she say her beloved is like?

She said her beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag.

title: Song of Songs 2:10 (#1)
content:
What did her beloved want her to do with him?

He wanted her to get up and come with him.

title: Song of Songs 2:11 (#1)
content:
What did he say was past, and what was over and gone?

He said the winter was gone and the rain had passed.

title: Song of Songs 2:12 (#2)
content:
For what is it time?

It is time for song.

title: Song of Songs 2:12 (#1)
content:
What has appeared in the land?

Flower blossoms have appeared in the land.

title: Song of Songs 2:13 (#2)
content:
What does her beloved want his beautiful one to do?

He wants her to arise and come with him.

title: Song of Songs 2:13 (#1)
content:
What ripens and what is in blossom?

The green fig tree ripens and the vines blossom.

title: Song of Songs 2:14 (#2)
content:
What does her beloved want to see and hear?

Her beloved wants to see her lovely appearance and hear her sweet voice.

title: Song of Songs 2:14 (#1)
content:
What does her beloved call her?

Her beloved calls her his dove.

title: Song of Songs 2:15 (#1)
content:
What does the woman want him to catch?

The woman wants him to catch the little foxes that ruin vineyards.

title: Song of Songs 2:16 (#1)
content:
To whom does the woman’s beloved belong?

Her beloved belongs to her.

title: Song of Songs 2:16 (#2)
content:
To whom does the woman belong?

She belongs to her beloved.

title: Song of Songs 2:16 (#3)
content:
What does her beloved do among the lilies?

He grazes among the lilies with pleasure.

title: Song of Songs 2:17 (#3)
content:
What does she want him to be like?

She wants him to be like a gazelle or a young stag on the rugged mountains.

title: Song of Songs 2:17 (#2)
content:
When does she want her beloved to turn?

She wants her beloved to turn to her until the soft winds of dawn blow and the shadows flee away.

title: Song of Songs 2:17 (#1)
content:
What does she want her beloved to do?

She wants her beloved to turn to her.

title: Song of Songs 3:1 (#1)
content:
For whom was the woman longing but could not find?

The woman was longing for the one whom she loved, but she could not find him.

title: Song of Songs 3:2 (#1)
content:
For whom did the woman search through the streets and squares but not find?

The woman searched through the streets and squares, but she could not find her beloved.

title: Song of Songs 3:3 (#1)
content:
What did the woman ask the watchmen when they found her?

She asked them, “Have you seen my beloved?”

title: Song of Songs 3:4 (#1)
content:
When did she find the one whom her soul loved?

She found the one whom her soul loved just after she passed the watchmen in the city.

title: Song of Songs 3:4 (#2)
content:
What did she do with her beloved?

She held him and would not let him go until she had brought him into her mother’s house.

title: Song of Songs 3:5 (#1)
content:
What does the woman want the daughters of Jerusalem to promise?

The woman wants the daughters of Jerusalem to promise they would not awaken or stir love before the right time.

title: Song of Songs 3:6–7 (#1)
content:
What does the young woman see coming from the wilderness that is perfumed with myrrh and frankincense and powders?

She sees the portable litter of Solomon coming with 60 warriors around it.

title: Song of Songs 3:8 (#1)
content:
At what were the warriors good?

The warriors were good with the sword and in warfare.

title: Song of Songs 3:9 (#1)
content:
What did King Solomon make for himself?

King Solomon made a sedan chair from wood from Lebanon.

title: Song of Songs 3:10 (#1)
content:
What did King Solomon’s sedan chair look like?

The chair had posts of silver, a back of gold, a seat of purple cloth, and was decorated and made comfortable with love from the daughters of Jerusalem.

title: Song of Songs 3:11 (#2)
content:
What was King Solomon wearing on his marriage day?

He wore a crown with which his mother crowned him on his marriage day.

title: Song of Songs 3:11 (#1)
content:
At what does the young woman want the women of Jerusalem to look?

She wants them to look at King Solomon.

title: Song of Songs 4:1 (#2)
content:
How does the woman’s lover describe her hair?

Her hair is like a flock of goats hopping down Mount Gilead.

title: Song of Songs 4:1 (#1)
content:
How does the woman’s lover describe her eyes?

Her eyes are as doves behind her veil.

title: Song of Songs 4:2 (#1)
content:
How does her lover describe her teeth?

Her teeth are like a flock of newly shorn and washed sheep, two of each and none missing.

title: Song of Songs 4:3 (#1)
content:
What does the woman’s beloved say about her lips and mouth?

He says that her lips are like a thread of scarlet and that her mouth is lovely.

title: Song of Songs 4:3 (#2)
content:
How does the woman’s beloved describe her cheeks?

He describes her cheeks as being like pomegranate halves behind her veil.

title: Song of Songs 4:4 (#1)
content:
How does the woman’s beloved describe her neck?

He describes her neck as the tower of David built in rows of stone with a thousand soldiers’ shields hanging on it.

title: Song of Songs 4:5 (#1)
content:
How does the woman’s beloved describe her two breasts?

He describes her two breasts as two fawns, twins of a gazelle, grazing among the lilies.

title: Song of Songs 4:6 (#1)
content:
Where will her lover go until dawn comes and the shadows flee?

He says he will go to the mountain of myrrh and the hill of frankincense.

title: Song of Songs 4:7 (#1)
content:
In what way is his love beautiful?

She is beautiful in every way.

title: Song of Songs 4:7 (#2)
content:
What does his beautiful love not have?

His beautiful love does not have any blemish.

title: Song of Songs 4:9 (#1)
content:
What does Solomon call his bride?

Solomon calls her his sister.

title: Song of Songs 4:10 (#1)
content:
What does Solomon say the love of his wife is better than?

Solomon says her love is better than wine.

title: Song of Songs 4:10 (#2)
content:
What is the smell of her perfume better than?

The smell of her perfume is better than any spice.

title: Song of Songs 4:11 (#2)
content:
What does the woman’s clothes smell like?

Her clothes smell like the fragrance of Lebanon.

title: Song of Songs 4:11 (#1)
content:
With what does he say his bride’s lips drip, and what is under her tongue?

He says his bride’s lips drip with nectar, and she has honey and milk under her tongue.

title: Song of Songs 4:12 (#1)
content:
What kind of garden and what kind of spring does Solomon say his sister, his bride, is like?

Solomon says she is like a garden locked up and a spring that is sealed.

title: Song of Songs 4:13–14 (#1)
content:
To what does he liken the woman’s shoots?

He likens her shoots to a grove of pomegranate trees with choice fruit and plants and all the finest spices.

title: Song of Songs 4:15 (#1)
content:
With what kinds of water does Solomon describe his lover?

He describes her as a garden spring, a well of fresh water, and streams flowing down from Lebanon.

title: Song of Songs 4:16 (#1)
content:
On what does the young woman want the north and south winds to blow and why?

She wants the north and south winds to blow on her garden so that its spices would give off their fragrance.

title: Song of Songs 4:16 (#2)
content:
What does she want her beloved to do and to eat?

She wants her beloved to come into his garden and to eat some of its choice fruit.

title: Song of Songs 5:1 (#1)
content:
Where has Solomon come?

Solomon has come into his garden.

title: Song of Songs 5:2 (#1)
content:
Of what is Solomon’s bride dreaming?

She is dreaming of her beloved’s knocking and talking.

title: Song of Songs 5:3 (#1)
content:
What has Solomon’s beloved already done?

She has already taken off her robe and washed her feet.

title: Song of Songs 5:4 (#1)
content:
Where had Solomon put his hand?

Solomon had put his hand through the opening of the door latch.

title: Song of Songs 5:5 (#1)
content:
With what were the bride’s hands dripping when she opened the door?

Her hands were dripping with moist myrrh.

title: Song of Songs 5:6 (#1)
content:
What did the bride find when she opened the door and how did she feel?

She found that her beloved had turned and gone, so her heart sank and she became sad.

title: Song of Songs 5:7 (#1)
content:
What did the watchmen do when they found Solomon’s bride?

They struck and wounded her and took away her veil.

title: Song of Songs 5:8 (#1)
content:
What does the bride ask the women of Jerusalem to promise?

She asks the women of Jerusalem to promise that if they find her beloved they will tell him she is lovesick for him.

title: Song of Songs 5:8 (#2)
content:
How does the young woman’s beloved make her feel?

The young woman’s beloved makes her feel sick with love.

title: Song of Songs 5:9 (#1)
content:
What do the young women ask of the bride?

They ask her how and why her beloved is better than another beloved.

title: Song of Songs 5:10 (#1)
content:
How does the young woman describe her beloved?

She describes him as radiant, ruddy, and outstanding.

title: Song of Songs 5:11 (#1)
content:
How does the woman describe her beloved’s head and hair?

She describes his head as pure gold and his hair as curly and black.

title: Song of Songs 5:12 (#1)
content:
How does the woman describe her beloved’s eyes?

She describes his eyes like doves washed in milk.

title: Song of Songs 5:13 (#1)
content:
How does Solomon’s bride describe his cheeks and lips?

She describes his cheeks like spice gardens and his lips like myrrh-soaked lilies.

title: Song of Songs 5:14 (#1)
content:
How does the woman describe her beloved’s arms and abdomen?

She describes his arms as rods of gold with topaz and his abdomen as a plate of ivory covered with sapphires.

title: Song of Songs 5:15 (#1)
content:
How does the woman describe her beloved’s legs and his appearance?

She describes his legs as marble pillars with gold bases and his appearance like Lebanon, as special as the cedars.

title: Song of Songs 5:16 (#1)
content:
How does Solomon’s bride describe her beloved’s mouth and Solomon himself to Jerusalem’s daughters?

She describes his mouth as most sweet and that Solomon is most desirable.

title: Song of Songs 6:1 (#1)
content:
What questions do the women of Jerusalem ask of the young woman?

They ask her where her beloved has gone and whether they can go with her to look for him.

title: Song of Songs 6:1 (#2)
content:
For what did the young women want to seek?

The young women wanted to seek for the young woman’s beloved.

title: Song of Songs 6:2 (#1)
content:
What does the young woman say her beloved was doing?

The young woman said he was in his spice gardens to graze in the garden and to gather lilies.

title: Song of Songs 6:3 (#2)
content:
Where does the young woman’s lover graze?

The young woman’s lover grazes among the lilies.

title: Song of Songs 6:3 (#1)
content:
To whom do the young woman and her lover belong?

The young woman and her lover belong to each other.

title: Song of Songs 6:4 (#1)
content:
What two cities does the woman’s lover use to describe her?

He describes her as two cities, Tirzah and Jerusalem.

title: Song of Songs 6:4 (#2)
content:
How does her beloved feel about her?

He feels that she is completely beautiful and lovely, but also awe-inspiring.

title: Song of Songs 6:5 (#2)
content:
How does the woman’s lover describe her hair?

He describes her hair as a flock of goats descending the slopes of Mount Gilead.

title: Song of Songs 6:5 (#1)
content:
Why does the woman’s lover want her to turn her eyes away from him?

The woman’s lover wants her to turn her eyes away from him because her eyes excite him.

title: Song of Songs 6:6 (#1)
content:
How does her lover describe her teeth?

He describes her teeth as a flock of ewes, each with twins and none missing, coming up from the washing place.

title: Song of Songs 6:7 (#1)
content:
How does her lover describe her cheeks?

Her lover describes her cheeks as pomegranate halves behind her veil.

title: Song of Songs 6:8 (#1)
content:
How many other women does the woman’s lover say there may be?

He says there may be 60 queens, 80 concubines, and young women without number.

title: Song of Songs 6:9 (#2)
content:
What did the queens and the concubines say about her when they saw her?

The queens and concubines called her blessed, and they praised her.

title: Song of Songs 6:9 (#1)
content:
How does the woman’s lover describe his dove?

The woman’s lover describes her as pure, the only one, and the special and favorite daughter of her mother.

title: Song of Songs 6:10 (#1)
content:
How does the woman’s lover describe her?

The woman’s lover describes her like the dawn, the moon, the sun, and as completely awesome.

title: Song of Songs 6:11 (#1)
content:
Why did the woman’s lover go into the grove of nut trees?

The woman’s lover went into the grove of nut trees to see if the vines had budded and the pomegranates were in bloom.

title: Song of Songs 6:12 (#1)
content:
How did the woman’s lover feel?

The woman’s lover felt as though he were riding in the chariot of a prince.

title: Song of Songs 6:13 (#3)
content:
What does the man ask the other people?

He asks why they look at her as if mesmerized by a dancer.

title: Song of Songs 6:13 (#2)
content:
Why does the woman’s lover want her to turn to him?

The woman’s lover wants her to turn to him so that he might gaze on her.

title: Song of Songs 6:13 (#1)
content:
What did the woman’s lover want her to do?

The woman’s lover wanted her to turn back to him.

title: Song of Songs 7:1 (#1)
content:
How does Solomon describe his lover’s feet in her sandals and the curves of her thighs?

He describes her feet in her sandals as beautiful and the curves of her thighs like the work of a craftsman.

title: Song of Songs 7:2 (#1)
content:
How does Solomon describe his love’s navel and belly?

Solomon describes his love’s navel as a round bowl which never lacks spiced wine and her belly as a mound of wheat surrounded with lilies.

title: Song of Songs 7:3 (#1)
content:
How does Solomon describe his lover’s two breasts?

Solomon describes her two breasts like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.

title: Song of Songs 7:4 (#1)
content:
How does Solomon describe his lover’s neck, eyes, and nose?

Solomon describes her neck as an ivory tower, her eyes like a pool, and her nose like the tower of Lebanon.

title: Song of Songs 7:5 (#1)
content:
How does Solomon describe his lover’s head and hair?

Solomon describes her head like Mount Carmel and her hair like purple, captivating him.

title: Song of Songs 7:7 (#1)
content:
How does Solomon describe his lover and her breasts?

He describes her height as a date palm tree and her breasts as date clusters.

title: Song of Songs 7:8 (#1)
content:
What does he also want his lover’s breasts and breath to be like?

He also wants his lover’s breasts to be like date clusters and her breath to be sweet like dates and the smell of an apple.

title: Song of Songs 7:9 (#1)
content:
What does he want his lover’s mouth to be like?

He wants her mouth to be like the best wine.

title: Song of Songs 7:10 (#1)
content:
To whom does the young woman belong and whom does he desire?

The young woman belongs to her beloved, and her beloved desires her.

title: Song of Songs 7:11 (#1)
content:
Where does the young woman want her beloved to go with her?

She wants him to go into the countryside to spend the night in the villages.

title: Song of Songs 7:12 (#1)
content:
Why does she want her beloved to rise early?

She wants him to rise early to see if the vines in the vineyards have budded and if the pomegranates have begun blooming.

title: Song of Songs 7:12 (#2)
content:
What does she say she will give to her beloved when they get to the vineyards?

She says she will give him her love.

title: Song of Songs 7:13 (#2)
content:
What does she say was at the door where she and her lover were staying?

She says that at the door where they were staying there were all sorts of choice fruits, new and old, that she had stored up for him.

title: Song of Songs 7:13 (#1)
content:
What does she say the mandrakes would do?

She says the mandrakes would give off their fragrance.

title: Song of Songs 8:1 (#1)
content:
What does the woman wish that her lover was like and why?

She wishes he were like her brother so that she could kiss her lover at any time and no one would despise her.

title: Song of Songs 8:2 (#1)
content:
Where would the woman have liked to bring her lover?

She would have liked to bring him to her mother’s house.

title: Song of Songs 8:3 (#1)
content:
What were her lover’s left and right hands doing?

His left hand was holding her head and his right hand was embracing her.

title: Song of Songs 8:4 (#1)
content:
What does the woman want Jerusalem’s women to promise?

The woman wants Jerusalem’s women to promise that they would not stir up love before its proper time.

title: Song of Songs 8:5 (#2)
content:
What did the young woman tell her lover when she woke him under the apple tree?

She told him that his mother had conceived and given birth to him under the apple tree.

title: Song of Songs 8:5 (#1)
content:
What do the women of Jerusalem ask?

They ask who is coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved.

title: Song of Songs 8:6 (#1)
content:
What does the young woman want her lover to do and why?

She wants him to set her as a seal over his heart, because love is as strong as death, and jealousy flashes like a hot flame.

title: Song of Songs 8:7 (#1)
content:
What could not stop love?

Floods of water could not put out the fire of love.

title: Song of Songs 8:8 (#1)
content:
What does the woman’s brothers say about their little sister?

They said that her breasts had not yet grown and that they wondered what they would do for her when she is promised in marriage.

title: Song of Songs 8:9 (#1)
content:
What would the woman’s brothers do if she were a wall?

If she were a wall, they would build a tower of silver on her.

title: Song of Songs 8:9 (#2)
content:
What would the woman’s brothers do if she were a door?

If she were a door, they would cover her with boards of cedar.

title: Song of Songs 8:10 (#1)
content:
How did the young woman describe herself?

She described herself as a wall with breasts large like towers, and completely mature.

title: Song of Songs 8:11 (#1)
content:
What did the young woman say that Solomon did with his vineyard at Baal Hamon?

Solomon leased his vineyard to those who would take care of it.

title: Song of Songs 8:12 (#1)
content:
What does the young woman say about her own vineyard and those who maintained it?

She said the 1000 shekels that it brought belonged to Solomon and that those who maintained it would get 200 shekels.

title: Song of Songs 8:13 (#1)
content:
What did the woman’s lover say to her who lived in the gardens, about what his friends, as well as he, wanted to hear?

He said that his friends, as well as he, wanted to be the ones to hear her voice.

title: Song of Songs 8:14 (#1)
content:
What does the young woman want her beloved to do and to be like?

She wants her beloved to hurry and to be like a deer.
